correctness.rationale: Splitting rate-one caller Poisson processes into directed edges gives independent undirected contact clocks of rate 1/a+1/b. Thus leaf/hub birth rates are h(b−l)c_b and (a−h)lc_b. On the s=√b·t scale the scaled leaf coordinate has drift h/a with vanishing quadratic variation and the hub jump intensity approaches (a−h)y/a; the finite-jump PDMP is uniquely constructed from integrated hazards and all hubs activate almost surely by finite scaled time. The first extra-hub time is the minimum of b independent two-stage Exp(c_b)+Exp((a−1)c_b) waits, with quadratic small-t cdf and Rayleigh scaling. Once hubs activate by o_P(1) time, b−o_P(b) leaves have independent Exp(1+a/b) residual clocks; conditional extreme-value limits give Gumbel independent of the early path. Rechecked exact birth rates and hypoexponential survival formulas for a=2,3,5 and b=1,4,20. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove J1 joint convergence.
residual_risks: The earlier literature already has the late Gumbel for fixed-size hub groups: only the early PDMP, exact first-extra-hub Rayleigh law and joint independence survive as new.
